conservation.condition_narrative: All paints appear secure and stable, with the exception of small edge losses. As the artist applied stiff, matte paints, spaces at edges or where one color abuts another, occasional "holidays" or areas of the board are visible. On the large leaf at the right edge, there is a small gouge, and near that is a small dent, but the surrounding paint appears stable. There are small edge losses, but overall, the paints on the surface are stable and secure. There are also frame abrasions along all four edges of the painting face where the work historically rested against the rabbet of O'Keeffe's original frame, and these are also normally expected in O'Keeffe's works from this period. Small bumps seen on the surface may be paint bit inclusions or may, in some cases, indicate the presence of lead soaps. Preliminary tests indicate little grime on the surface.
conservation.technical_description:
**Support:** The support is a composite wood fiber panel, textured on one side, smooth on the other. The artist has painted on the smooth side. The board appears to be stable and in good plane. There are minor edge losses due to previous framing. 
 
 
 
**Ground or Support Preparation:** There is no indication that the artist added sizing to the board surface prior to painting. It also appears that no ground layer was applied, but rather, the artist painted in oils directly onto the bare board. Many areas of bare board are visible below the paint layers. 
 
 
 
**Design Layers:** There does not appear to be graphite underdrawing, though it may be entirely covered by the paint application. The artist has prepared her higher-value whites and lighter colors to achieve a slightly stiff, cream-like consistency. The background (off-white), in particular, has the appearance of being "troweled" on using a palette knife, giving a textural effect. Darker values, by contrast, were prepared with more fluid, cream consistencies, but are more paste-like, whereas lighter values have been applied. O'Keeffe applies paint at the margins of forms using nearly continuous, curvilinear brush strokes with the brush positioned at a low angle to the support, resulting in a continuous, raised ridge of paint at the edge of each form. Surrounding brushwork is generally parallel to the linear directions defined by these edges, with no underlying or subsequent brushwork moving perpendicular to the linear form. Occasionally, adjacent forms do not overlap, and the artist has chosen to allow a "holiday" of the unprimed board to be a visible detail in the composition. The sides of the board have also been painted in oil in some areas as a carryover from the design, while in other sections, they merely suggest the compositional colors without direct contact with the color adjacent in the design. Small bumps seen on the surface may be paint bit inclusions or may, in some cases, indicate the presence of lead soaps. 
 
   
 
**Surface Coating:** The painting appears to have no varnish coating. 
 
 
 
**Framing, Backing, and Hanging Hardware:** The work is framed in a contemporary, micro-environmentally buffered, and gasketed metal-leaf "clam shell" profile frame, a reproduction of O'Keeffe's original design, created by framer/artist George Of. The glazing is Optium® tin salt-coated, UV-absorbing, static-free, non-reflective acrylic. The Optium glazing has a Volara closed-cell polyethylene gasket/pad. The frame is fitted with a laminated, Volara-gasketed backing strainer, which has a Security mirror-hanger and T-bolt hardware as well as D-rings.
